answers.q1: It does not look like one surface changing size/role. Frames 001/003/005 show the Tailscale app (device list) plus a terminal window underneath, with a system 'Python network access' permission dialog overlaid. Between 005 and 007 the entire screen content is replaced: the Tailscale window and terminal are gone, and a completely different app (a meeting recorder UI with '14:50の会議', 決まったこと/やること panels, 文字起こし panel) fills the same screen area, with the same permission dialog now floating over it instead. Between 011 and 013 the screen swaps back to the Tailscale+terminal view. This reads as a hard cut between two unrelated windows/apps, not a single surface morphing or resizing.
answers.q2: Within the meeting app itself (007→009→011) there is no layout shift: the timer, panel headers, and placeholder-to-content text occupy the same positions and line heights. However, at the scene level there is a large jump: the whole content composition (sidebar/list layout of Tailscale vs. the three-column meeting layout) changes abruptly with no intermediate/blended frame, and then jumps back again later. The permission dialog itself stays pixel-identical in position across all frames regardless of what is behind it.
answers.q3: No frame shows a broken half-rendered state (no partial paint, no missing icons/text mid-draw). But because the transition from the Tailscale/terminal scene to the meeting-app scene (and back) happens with no visible in-between frame, it plays like an instant pop/cut rather than a smooth change — this can read as a flicker/scene-swap rather than a continuous transition.
answers.q4: Within the meeting app there is clear feedback: the recording timer advances (00:01→00:02), and the 決まったこと/やること sections update from 'waiting' placeholders to real content ('導入時期は10月で行います', '見積は明日までにお願いします'), and the 文字起こし panel is visibly empty ('まだ発話がありません') during this span. But the permission dialog itself gives zero feedback — it is static, unchanged, and unexplained across the entire sequence, sitting on top of both unrelated scenes.
answers.q5: The transcript/decision-list filling in is purposeful animation-adjacent feedback that explains recording progress. The full-scene swaps between the Tailscale/terminal view and the meeting UI do not explain anything — they look like unrelated background windows being captured, not a purposeful transition tied to the meeting-start action.
answers.q6: The scene-level jump (005→007 and 011→013) would feel abrupt if it represented a real UI transition — there's no eased/animated hand-off, just a cut. Also, the permission dialog is present, unresolved, and covering roughly the right half of the meeting UI (including the transcription and action buttons) for the entire visible recording duration, which would feel like an intrusive, unresolved interruption at exactly the moment the user wants to see the meeting state.

observations.what: No visible change; identical Tailscale/terminal scene with permission dialog, same cursor position.
No visible change; terminal log text unchanged, dialog unchanged.

Hard scene swap: Tailscale+terminal view is fully replaced by the meeting recorder UI ('14:50の会議', 録音中 00:01). Permission dialog persists but now floats over the new scene in the same screen position.
Meeting UI persists; only the recording timer advances 00:01→00:02. No layout change.
決まったこと and やること placeholders are replaced with real entries ('導入時期は10月で行います' / '見積は明日までにお願いします'). Text panel positions unchanged, no shift.
Hard scene swap back: meeting UI is fully replaced by the Tailscale+terminal view again; permission dialog persists unchanged, terminal elapsed-time label reads 7s.
No visible change beyond terminal elapsed-time label incrementing 7s→8s; scene otherwise static.

weaknesses.what: The two scenes (Tailscale/terminal vs. meeting UI) swap in and out with no visible connecting motion — reads as separate windows being switched, not one surface changing role.
weaknesses.fix: If this is meant to show the app surface transforming into the meeting view, capture/animate an actual intermediate state (resize, cross-fade, or shared-element morph) so it reads as continuity rather than a window swap.

weaknesses.what: The instant full-scene pop between very different layouts with no intermediate frame reads as a jarring cut/flicker when played back.
weaknesses.fix: Add an eased transition (fade or scale) between the two scenes so the change is legible as a state change rather than a cut.

weaknesses.what: The 'Python' network-access permission dialog is present, static, and unexplained for the entire captured span, overlapping meeting content without any acknowledgement or resolution shown.
weaknesses.fix: Resolve or reposition the permission prompt before/independently of the meeting-start flow so it doesn't sit indefinitely on top of the primary UI during the moment being judged.

weaknesses.what: The scene-level jump between Tailscale/terminal and the meeting UI carries no explanatory motion — it doesn't help the viewer understand what triggered the change.
weaknesses.fix: Tie the transition visually to the triggering action (e.g., a launching/expanding animation from a dock icon or button) so the cut has narrative motion behind it.
